title: Deployment gate — evidence automation & RBAC v2 roadmap
content:
Purpose:
This working note captures a pragmatic roadmap and lightweight checklist to bring RBAC v2 attestation, audit-log schema validation, and evidence automation into the deployment gate for go-live decisions. It is intentionally slightly informal — use as the basis for creating a more formal Runbook once we validate the automation primitives.

Scope and goals:
- Scope: production deployment gates for hosted and dedicated clusters (includes Private with customer-managed control plane). Excludes: non-prod experiments.
- Goals: reduce manual evidence collection time during a deployment security review from hours to minutes; ensure RBAC v2 coverage checks and audit-log exports are repeatable and machine-verifiable; provide a clear exception approval path for time-limited deviations.

High-level roadmap (quarterly milestones):
- Q1: Lightweight verifier prototypes: RBAC surface scanner + audit log schema checker + SIEM export smoke tests. Minimal CLI that exports an evidence bundle.
- Q2: Integrate with CI/CD: attach evidence bundles to release artifacts; simple webhook to shiproom. Automatic preflight gate in pipeline (opt-in for initially low-risk services).
- Q3: Policy automation: map higher-level release policies (least privilege required, retention limits) into RBAC test cases and SIEM parsers.
- Q4: Exception engine & approvals UI: allow short-lived exceptions with automated compensation controls and one-click evidence attach.

Key deliverables for the prototype (Q1):
1) RBAC v2 surface scanner (poC):
   - Enumerate roles, role bindings, resource scopes for the service namespace(s).
   - Produce a CSV/JSON listing: role, binding type, principal, resource(s), actions allowed (read/write/exec).
   - Flag any wildcard permissions (e.g., '*' on resources or verbs) for manual review.
   - Output a short human-readable summary for the reviewer.
   - Owner: eng-security; acceptance: output exists and runs against staging cluster.

2) Audit log schema checker:
   - Baseline schema fields we validate for deployment evidence: event_time (RFC3339), event_id (uuid), actor.id, actor.type, resource.id, resource.type, action, outcome (success/fail), request_id/correlation_id, pre_state_hash, post_state_hash, raw_payload_snippet (optional).
   - Tool should scan a sample of logs for schema compliance and timestamp skew, check for missing correlation ids, and verify retention flag metadata if present.
   - Generate a short report: total events sampled, pct compliant, top 10 missing fields, sample non-compliant event lines.
   - Owner: observability team; acceptance: run against last 24h export from pre-prod and produce report.

3) SIEM export smoke test:
   - Verify that our SIEM ingest mapping contains required fields and that parsers correctly annotate actor/resource. Provide both Splunk and ELK example queries.
   - Minimal checks: field mapping exists, timestamp parsing correct, correlation id trace works across services, alerts trigger for admin role changes.
   - Output: pass/fail + pointer to failing parser lines.

4) Evidence bundle format (proto for handoff):
   - Bundle pieces (zipped): rbac-scan.json, audit-schema-report.txt, siem-smoke.json, deployment-config.yaml, signed-commit-hash.txt, checklist.md
   - Each bundle MUST include a checksum file and a signer identity (who executed the bundle creation).

Lightweight preflight checklist (use this in shiproom or CI failures):
- RBAC checks:
  - [ ] RBAC scanner run with target namespace(s)
  - [ ] No role contains wildcard verbs across sensitive resources (flagged entries reviewed)
  - [ ] Service accounts used by the deployment have minimally scoped roles
  - [ ] Human owners for any cross-namespace bindings documented

- Audit logs:
  - [ ] Audit export for the last 24h available and included in evidence bundle
  - [ ] Events for any recent privilege changes present and validated
  - [ ] event_time values within acceptable clock skew (<= 5s for same region)
  - [ ] correlation_id present on >= 95% of sampled events

- SIEM & alerting:
  - [ ] SIEM parser matched key event types in smoke test
  - [ ] Test alert for admin-role-change fired end-to-end
  - [ ] Retention policy metadata exists and aligns with minimum retention SLA

- Exception gating (if any check failed):
  - [ ] An open exception request ticket exists (JIRA key)
  - [ ] Exception duration and compensating controls documented
  - [ ] Exception approver (security manager or delegated approver) signed off

Exception approval flow (lightweight):
1) Submit exception request in JIRA using template (SEC-EXC-TEMPLATE): include scope, risk notes, compensating controls, duration, and automated mitigations (e.g., increased logging, temporary deny-lists).
2) Auto-notify: security-oncall + product-owner + SRE owner.
3) For short lived (< 72 hours) low-risk exceptions: delegated approver can approve via single-step comment. For anything longer/higher-risk: require security manager sign-off and a secondary SRE approver.
4) Every approved exception must auto-produce a follow-up evidence snapshot at exception end and a post-mortem entry.

Approval template (copyable into JIRA description):
- Summary: [one-liner]
- Affected services/namespaces: [list]
- Check failing: [rbac | audit | siem | other]
- Risk impact: [low|med|high] and rationale
- Compensating controls: [e.g., increased sampling, temporary deny, manual review cadence]
- Duration requested: [hours/days]
- Approver (role): [name / role]
- Post-exception tasks: [evidence snapshot, verify parsers, rollback plan]

Acceptance sign-off template (to attach to evidence bundle):
- Service: [name]
- Version/commit: [sha]
- Deployed at: [timestamp]
- RBAC scan: PASS/FLAGGED (attach rbac-scan.json)
- Audit schema check: PASS/FAIL (attach audit-schema-report.txt)
- SIEM smoke: PASS/FAIL (attach siem-smoke.json)
- Security approver: [name + timestamp]
- SRE approver: [name + timestamp]

Operational snippets (for quick verification):
- Basic RBAC surface dump (kubectl example):
  kubectl get roles,rolebindings,clusterroles,clusterrolebindings -A -o json | jq '.items[] | {kind: .kind, metadata: .metadata.name, rules: .rules}' > rbac-raw.json
  (run rbac scanner against rbac-raw.json)

- Quick audit schema check (example jq):
  jq -r 'select(.event_time == null or .event_id == null) | {line: ., path: .path}' audit_export.json | head -n 20

- Splunk example (pseudo):
  index=audit sourcetype="redwood:audit" | stats count by action, actor.type | where count > 0

- Kibana (ELK) example to ensure correlation ends up in same trace: trace.id: "<sample>" AND event.action: "privilege.grant"

SIEM field mapping (minimal required fields):
- timestamp -> event_time
- id -> event_id
- actor_id -> actor.id
- actor_type -> actor.type
- resource_id -> resource.id
- action -> action
- outcome -> outcome
- correlation_id -> correlation_id
- raw -> raw_payload_snippet

Evidence automation implementation notes:
- Prefer idempotent bundle creators: run multiple times -> identical bundle if no system change. Use signed commits and signer id to assert provenance.
- Keep sample size configurable (default 1k events) for first run; increase during larger releases if needed.
- Use a circuit breaker: if SIEM export fails consistently, fail the preflight unless an exception is in place.
- For Private deployments: include instructions to fetch local SIEM endpoint details for mapping; treat KMS/HSM evidence as separate attachment pointers (not in-bundle).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- What granularity do we want for role-level attestation? service-account only, or also human operator bindings?
- PSI: define acceptable clock skew for cross-region deployments (>5s?).
- Should we require encrypted-in-transit evidence bundles for all external auditors?

Next steps (immediate):
- Diego: prototype RBAC scanner script and drop in /tmp/rbac-proto.json (due 2024-12-05).
- Priya: build the audit schema checker minimal implementation and sample report (due 2024-12-12).
- Samir: stub SIEM smoke test harness with Splunk and ELK queries (due 2025-01-05).
- Security team: review exception template and sign-off flow by 2025-01-10 so we can fast-follow CI integration.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working doc intended to converge into a runbook. Please annotate where we should make the checks stricter or introduce automation earlier. Link any related incident writeups or PRs into linked_artifacts so we can close the feedback loop.

Revision history:
- 2024-11-20: initial draft (Ava K.)
- 2024-12-06: added RBAC scanner acceptance criteria (Diego)
- 2025-01-12: updated exception flow and sign-off template post-discussion (Priya)
